svg.text: F. An arena through both poles
The circle through a land touch-down and both poles: a stretch of sea ice, a stretch of ice sheet, and what lies between. From the prototype (seed 7).
Whole arena (153,600 units; heights exaggerated); T in the middle
The north pole, 24,000 units each way: the pack thick at the pole, thinning and parting toward its edge (heights exaggerated 30 times)
The south pole, 24,000 units each way: the ice sheet rises gently toward the pole (about true scale), the shelf, then open water
What a fighter sees: one screen (3,000 units), to scale
North, 3,000 from the pole: big floes, thick
North, near the edge of the pack: an iceberg in open water
South, 3,000 from the pole: the dome of the ice sheet
South, 12,500 from the pole: the shelf and its cliff
Sea ice: flat white platforms a few units above the water (10 to 40), hundreds to a few thousand units across, with dark water between. Bergs stand 45
to 215 units: taller than a fighter. No buildings, no people: no collateral at all.
Ice sheet: a long white slope that rises 1,500 to 2,500 units toward the pole, rock showing through the high ground; at the coast a flat shelf 36
units high that ends in a cliff. Also nothing built.
New rules this would ask for (not built): ice is thin, so a crater through a floe should open the water under it (today water only exists where the
original ground is below the sea); fighters can dive into the leads (the ocean cover rule already exists).
